why_math: Monte Carlo sampling averages many noisy light-impact measurements, and adding more samples shrinks the error predictably—the neural network then learns to interpolate this noisy truth smoothly, becoming differentiable and orders of magnitude faster.

A delta-function boundary lives in measure-zero space; blurring it with a kernel expands this slim region into an ordinary volume where normal sampling works, much like photon mapping avoids trying to hit point lights directly.

Quadrature cost scales with particle count in standard MPM; fixing quadrature points on the grid and resampling to them makes the solver cost independent of particles—particles become just history carriers, not integration rules.

Spherical harmonics encode low-frequency content sparsely; converting to a grid, multiplying point-wise, and converting back trades a hard closed-form product for simple arithmetic, with grid resolution determining the exact-vs-approximate trade-off.

Flip operations alone fail at flip-hard configurations; inserting and moving interior Steiner points strategically breaks those deadlocks, and finite-precision fixes prevent topology corruption in rounding errors.

Monte Carlo solves both the rendering equation and the wave integral at once—each light ray path contributes to both radiance and phase simultaneously, converging smoothly to physical accuracy as sample count grows.

Holographic color distortion is a composition of known optical and sensor nonlinearities; modeling each source (laser coherence, modulator limits, aberration, camera bias) and correcting it jointly recovers perceptual fidelity.

Tracking reference motions alone overfits to narrow styles; adversarial learning adds a critic that penalizes bad actions in novel contexts, forcing the policy to learn reusable principles that compose and generalize.

Rough DOE phase profiles lose light; encoding only the amplitude part and smoothing the phase profile to sinusoidal shapes reduces scattering loss—spatial frequency band-division then splits colors without crosstalk.

Floating-point errors in CCD come from two sources: approximate coefficients and rounding in arithmetic; decomposing them separately reveals how each propagates, enabling structured error bounds and rigorous robustness.
Kinematic deployability of hinged kirigami is a system of geometric constraints—deriving them for arbitrary planar graphs yields the full space of valid face orientations and degrees of freedom.

Two synchronized laser paths share the rendering burden cooperatively, each independently forming volumetric voxels; parallel operation increases total voxel density and brightness without the single-path power bottleneck.

Rough surface scattering is a convolution of the hidden scene with a spatial filter; learning that kernel explicitly from measurements narrows the space of plausible reconstructions, improving generalization over pure end-to-end learning.

Crease patterns are periodic structures; homogenization theory extracts macroscopic effective stiffness by folding a unit cell and averaging its energy, revealing how local geometry sculpts global mechanical anisotropy.
